newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market quiet ahead of new cash reserve.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market quiet ahead of new cash reserve.

text.p: Most Dutch money market rates were unchanged in quiet trading on Wednesday.
Most activity was reported in overnight money and deposits of up to two weeks and one month.
Call money was quoted between 3.12 and 3.18 percent bid, and traders said most deals were done near those levels.
On Tuesday, call money had been bid as high as 3.50 percent as several market players had been seeking money ahead of the cash reserve expiry at the end of the week.

Although the situation was back to normal today, dealers said overnight rates could start fluctuating again if market players concluded they were in need of additional money in order to avoid having to pay 4.5 percent on any negative cash balance.
"And rates can move very easily in such a market," one said.
On Friday, a new cash reserve arrangement, running until August 22, takes effect.
Indicative prices for Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) were all unchanged from Tuesday and were still out of line with market prices.
Dealers said they had not heard of any trade in DTCs.
They did not expect the special advances rate to be moved on Thursday when a new pact will be announced.
Persistent guilder weakness against the mark had led to a 0.10 percent hike in the rate to 3.00 percent on July 10, making it level with Germany's equivalent repo rate.
The guilder was trading at 112.57/58 per 100 marks, below the 112.673 ERM central rate.
